title: Hybrid primitive stubs and output shims — design proposal
content:
Purpose
This note proposes a lightweight, backwards-compatible pattern for evolving Terraform primitives used by Redwood Private: a combination of minimal "stub" primitives plus explicit output shims and compatibility adapters. The goal is to enable non-breaking rollout of VPC/IAM/cluster module changes across hosted, dedicated, and on-prem deployments while keeping state migrations safe and reviewable.

Motivation / pain we see
- Large modules ballooned with provider-specific logic (GKE vs EKS vs AKS) and optional outputs, making changes risky.
- Breaking changes surface late during customer upgrades because downstream stacks depended on implicit outputs/side-effects.
- One-off hacks (shadow outputs, terraform locals in consumers) lead to brittle rollbacks.
- On-prem clusters complicate test matrices; we need a low-risk path for incremental interface evolution.

Design principles
1) Keep primitive interfaces minimal and explicit: each primitive (vpc, subnet, iam-roles, cluster-core, nodepool) exposes a small, well-documented set of variables and outputs.
2) Compatibility via shims: introduce dedicated "shim" modules in the same repo that translate old outputs/inputs to new ones; these are lightweight and have separate versioning.
3) Non-invasive state migration: prefer adapter modules that read existing resources (data sources) and produce the new outputs without destructive resource replacement.
4) Clear versioning policy: semantic module versions, with a documented migration step for patch->minor and minor->major.
5) Test-first rollout: automated acceptance tests per primitive and per shim, exercised in a staging env that mirrors on-prem variants.

Primitive surface-level spec (proposed minimal interfaces)
- vpc-primitive variables: name, cidr_blocks (list), tags (map), enable_flow_logs (bool), shared_services_subnet_ids (list). Outputs: vpc_id, primary_cidr, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids, route_table_ids, flow_log_ids.
- iam-primitive variables: namespace, service_account_mappings (map), assume_role_trusts (map), tags. Outputs: role_arns (map), sa_iam_bindings (map), iam_policy_document_json (string).
- cluster-core variables: cluster_name, control_plane_subnet_ids (list), cluster_version, platform (enum: eks|gke|aks|onprem). Outputs: cluster_id, api_endpoint, kubeconfig (sensitive), control_plane_security_group_id.
- nodepool-primitive variables: nodepool_name, instance_profile, desired_count, taints, autoscaling (object-as-map). Outputs: nodepool_ids, node_role_arn, node_security_group_ids.

Shim/adapter pattern (how compatibility works)
- For each breaking interface change, create a shim module named shim/<primitive>-vX-to-vY. The shim: reads the new primitive outputs and emits the legacy output keys expected by older consumers. It is pinned with its own version and documented as a migration helper.
- Example: Previously consumers relied on 'vpc.private_subnets' (list of maps). New primitive emits 'private_subnet_ids' (list of ids) and 'subnet_meta' (map keyed by id). The shim exposes 'private_subnets' by doing a lookup in subnet_meta and reconstructing the older shape.
- Shims are intentionally pure: they avoid creating resources; they only transform outputs and optionally read resources with data sources to fill gaps. This minimizes state churn.

Variable and output naming conventions
- Use stable prefixes: primitive_<name>_id or <primitive>_id only for single ids; plural forms end with _ids; maps end with _map or _meta.
- Avoid nested complex objects as outputs where possible. If required, provide both compact id lists and a metadata map.
- Backwards-compatible aliases: new outputs should include both the canonical new name and, optionally, an alias name that matches older consumers for one release cycle. Example: 'private_subnet_ids' + 'private_subnets_v1' (deprecated).

Versioning and deprecation lifecycle
- Patch (x.y.z -> x.y.z+): non-breaking bugfixes. No consumer churn.
- Minor (x.y -> x.y+1): additive changes only (new variables/outputs). Provide shim when necessary for older consumers. Keep aliases for one minor release and add deprecation warnings in docs.
- Major (x -> x+1): breaking changes. Require: migration docs, shim module, an automated state validation plan, and at least 2-week canary window.

Upgrade plan template (for a given primitive)
1) Author new primitive version in feature branch. Add unit tests + acceptance tests.
2) Publish shim module that maps from new outputs back to old shape. Add examples showing consumer replacement.
3) Create PR to bump consumers in internal stacks (console, dedicated) to reference shim first, then migrate consumers to new outputs incrementally.
4) Run integration test suite on staging clusters (cloud + on-prem emulator). Validate no replacements occur.
5) Nightly run terraform plan for a cohort of non-prod tenants to detect drift.
6) Schedule a canary upgrade on low-risk customer clusters; monitor logs/metrics for 48–72h.
7) If green, document deprecation timeline and remove shim aliases after two minor releases.

State migration guidance (do's and don'ts)
- DO use data sources to discover existing resources rather than re-creating them.
- DO provide a dry-run checklist: terraform plan with -out, save json plan, run plan-drift tooling.
- DO break changes into N small steps (introduce new outputs, introduce shim, migrate consumers, remove shim aliases).
- DON'T change resource identities (names/tags/ids) in the same release where you change interfaces.
- DON'T rely on consumers to be updated at the same time as the primitive change. Shims exist for that reason.

Testing and CI requirements
- Unit tests for any helper logic in modules (terragrunt/terraform test harness).
- Acceptance tests per provider: e2e for EKS/GKE/AKS and a lightweight on-prem harness (kubeadm or kind?) that exercises kubeconfig and nodepool APIs.
- A matrix job in CI that runs terraform plan against representative consumer stacks using the shim and without shim to validate plan neutrality.
- A nightly "upgrade simulation" job: switch consumers from old->shim->new and capture any plan changes.

Example consumer migration snippet (conceptual)
- Old: module.vpc = source "git::.../vpc?ref=v1"
- New interim: module.vpc_new = source "git::.../vpc?ref=v2"
  module.vpc_compat = source "git::.../shim/vpc-v1-to-v2?ref=v1"
  consumers reference module.vpc_compat.private_subnets
- Later: update consumers to reference module.vpc_new.private_subnet_ids and remove vpc_compat.

Operational checklist for on-prem customers
- Preflight: inventory existing tags and resource names; capture terraform state snapshot.
- Test: apply in an air-gapped staging environment if available.
- Fallback: have documented steps to re-pin module refs and re-run terraform apply to return to previous stable state.
- Support: schedule a live run with solutions engineering for first three upgrades of major changes.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide policy for how long to keep alias outputs (proposed: two minor releases).
- Determine storage/retention for archived terraform plans from upgrade simulations.
- Confirm on-prem acceptance test harness technology (we have prototypes using kind + cloud emulators; need infra budget approval).
- Draft a short customer-facing KB that explains what to expect during minor vs major upgrades.

Appendix: small examples and naming recommendations
- Good: vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, subnet_meta_map, flow_log_ids
- Avoid: private_subnets (list of complex maps) unless accompanied by private_subnet_ids
- Shim pattern: shim/vpc-v1-to-v2 — no resource creates, only output mapping + optional data lookups

Notes to self (rough)
- We'll spin up a prototype shim for vpc change in a spike branch.
- Pair with QA to write the upgrade simulation job next sprint.
- Invite infra-qa + solutions-eng to a working session 2026-03-05 (time TBD).

End of doc.
